newsitem.title: ITALY: Telecom Italia ready to buy 20 pct of Seat. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Telecom Italia ready to buy 20 pct of Seat. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: Italian telecommunications group Telecom Italia said on Friday that it was ready to buy up to 20 percent of the ordinary shares in Seat, a telephone directory unit of state telecom holding Stet.
State holding company IRI, which controls Stet, has said it wants to spin off Seat by the end of the year. Stet is slated for privatisation by March 31, 1997.
An extraordinary meeting of Stet is due to take place on Monday (Corrects from Saturday).
The extraordinary meeting is due to decide on the split of Seat from Stet.
Following the split, IRI will hold some 60 percent of Seat with the remainder floated on the stock market.
IRI has already received 26 suitable offers from Seat from both Italian and foreign offers.
Telecom Italia said in a statement that once such a sale had been carried out it was ready to take a "minority stake of not more than 20 percent" of Seat's ordinary capital.
Analysts believe Seat could be worth more than $2 billion.
Newspapers have reported that U.S. telephone company GTE, British Telecom and France Telecom are all interested in Seat.
